signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Crowded Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.17, holding just below its SMA20 of 159.19 while the 200-hour MA serves as a tactical ceiling. The Pentagon has signaled it is not ruling out military force in the Strait of Hormuz, introducing a geopolitical risk premium that conflicts with the structural 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. Options markets are aggressively hedging downside risk with the 1M 25d risk reversal at -1.96, a level showing strong demand for JPY protection despite the carry-supportive backdrop. Speculative positioning shows JPY net shorts at -73,641, creating a crowded environment vulnerable to a disorderly unwind if geopolitical tensions spike. JPY's safe-haven function is currently distorted, with USD/JPY vs VIX correlation at +0.435 (z=+2.06σ), suggesting carry remains the dominant driver until a major volatility breakout. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; carry support is offset by acute intervention and geopolitical risks. Catalyst: US-Iran escalation headlines. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, restoring JPY safe-haven flows and forcing a carry liquidation.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Drag
signals.text: AUD/CHF is the primary G10 bilateral theme with a 1.071% performance spread between the week's leader and laggard. AUD 1W average strength sits at +0.686% across 4 pairs, while CHF has weakened by -0.385% despite its typical safe-haven profile. The Australian Dollar's outperformance is currently testing headwinds from new Iran sanctions, which have begun to sour risk appetite and pull the pair off recent two-month highs. A massive +435bp carry advantage for AUD vs CHF remains the fundamental anchor, though COT positioning for AUD is becoming elevated at a 52-week percentile of 81. Retail sentiment is extremely short AUD/USD at 88%, providing a contrarian cushion against institutional profit-taking. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry advantage dominates provided risk sentiment does not undergo a systemic collapse. Catalyst: RBA Meeting Minutes on 25 August. Risk: Sustained geopolitical escalation drives a classic flight to CHF, neutralizing the carry premium.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Extreme + Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3638, positioned well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3400-1.3502), marking a clean bullish technical profile. However, CFTC data shows speculative long positioning is reaching extreme levels with a 52-week percentile of 94 and a z-score of +1.45, suggesting the move is becoming crowded. This institutional positioning is met by an extreme retail short bias of 83%, creating a squeeze scenario if price extends. The options market is pricing in significant uncertainty, evidenced by a massive +5.2% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 5.8%), the highest in the G10 space. This elevated hedging demand suggests that while the trend remains bullish, market participants are paying a steep premium for protection against a trend reversal. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; momentum remains intact but high VRP suggests limited near-term upside without a fresh catalyst. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: LF net long reversal begins to align with negative ESI (-8.3), triggering a profit-taking liquidation.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ESI Divergence + Restrictive Real Rates
signals.text: EUR/USD is holding at 1.1671, maintaining a position above its SMA200 (1.1635) and both its SMA20 and SMA50. The pair is supported by a widening divergence in economic data trends, as the Eurozone ESI shows a moderate positive bias (+9.6) against the US ESI's strong negative print of -15.7. While the nominal carry favors the USD by +135bp, the real policy rate differential is much tighter at +1.41% (USD +1.48% vs EUR +0.07%), reducing the structural incentive to hold dollars as US data persists in missing expectations. COT data shows leveraged funds remain net short EUR (-76,035), placing them at the 10th percentile of the 52-week range, which suggests significant room for a short-covering rally if the ECB's hawkish bias is reaffirmed. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD; contrarian to crowded spec shorts and supported by US data underperformance. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — Hike bias priced. Risk: US 10Y yields rebound sharply on geopolitical safe-haven bids, re-asserting the nominal carry advantage.
